question: What does the manual recommend when a pump makes a gravel-like noise?
final_answer:
The pump manual recommends checking the suction pressure, which must remain above 0.5 bar to ensure sufficient Net Positive Suction Head (NPSH), as a gravel-like noise indicates cavitation (manual: pump_manual.pdf p.2). 

Additional corrective actions listed for this symptom include performing a laser alignment (maximum offset 0.05 mm) and replacing the bearing kit (SP-PMP-BRG-62) while inspecting the impeller for erosion (manual: pump_manual.pdf p.2).

•  Pump/motor misalignment
•  Worn pump bearings or damaged impeller
Corrective actions:
1. Check suction pressure: it must stay above 0.5 bar. A gravel-like noise indicates cavitation.
2. Perform laser alignment (max offset 0.05 mm).
3. Replace the bearing kit SP-PMP-BRG-62 and inspect the impeller for erosion.

3. Measure phase voltages; imbalance above 2% must be corrected by the electrical team.

•  Clogged downstream filter

Corrective actions:
1. Check all discharge valve positions against the P&ID.
2. Measure differential pressure across the downstream filter; replace the element SP-PMP-FLT-80 if it
exceeds 0.8 bar.
3. Never operate the pump against a closed valve for more than 30 seconds.
